prompt: At a rate of $4$ tickets for \$$10$, how much do $14$ tickets cost?
hint: Four does not multiply neatly to fourteen, so find what one ticket costs and build up from there.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Try halving the deal: if $4$ tickets cost $10$ dollars, what do $2$ tickets cost? Can you make $14$ out of groups of $4$ and $2$?
Four does not multiply neatly to fourteen, so find what one ticket costs and build up from there.
One ticket costs $10 \div 4 = 2.50$ dollars. Multiply that unit price by $14$ tickets.
$14 \times 2.50 = 35$, so the cost of $14$ tickets is $35$ dollars.

explanation: Find the unit rate by dividing cost by tickets: $10 \div 4 = 2.50$ dollars per ticket.
Multiply by the number of tickets wanted, since every ticket costs the same: $14 \times 2.50$.
Work it in pieces: $14 \times 2 = 28$ and $14 \times 0.50 = 7$, and $28 + 7 = 35$.
The cost of fourteen tickets is $35$ dollars.
